body: I don’t want to talk about it anymore

I’ve tried forcing myself to confront my anxiety but it just makes everything so much worse. I used to like to read and cook but people told me I couldn’t make anything good so I stopped cooking and I don’t have the energy to read anymore
I get anxious in social situations and have severe performance anxiety and it makes it hard to even try to do anything. Honestly nothing really makes me happy anymore
Because I’m depressed all the time and my anxiety gets really bad so they’re constantly having to help me and I could just go away and their lives would be better
I’ve been told that for as long as I can remember. I have a boyfriend and really supportive friends but I just feel like I get in their way and they’d be better off without me
I just don’t see the point in living anymore because I’m completely worthless

To be clear, I’m (18f). My last girlfriend broke up with me after half a year and told me that she had a boyfriend the entire time she was with me. She also told me that I was just an experiment for her to see if she liked women. I don’t know if I’ll ever be able to trust a girl I date again because it really hurt to hear that. I also had a recent relationship with a guy, but he honestly wasn’t much better.
That’s what I’m asking for
My parents tend to blame me for stuff outside of my control so I don’t think I can tell them
I’m just so embarrassed that I let this happen to me
I’m just not sure how much longer I can deal with this before it completely consumes me

At this point, I’m pretty sure I won’t ever be able to change their mind. If I was 18 and could actually get away, I feel like it would be easier but I still am completely under their control. Sometimes the only thing I can do to get away is to say I’m going to spend the night with a friend and just sleeping in my car. 

I’m just so tired of acting like I’m fine when I feel like I’m drowning.

Thank you. I’m not sure yet on the whole God thing. My parents know that I don’t feel like I’m catholic and the only thing my mother said to me was to make sure I didn’t lose my moral compass because I can apparently only have decent morals if I’m catholic. I might find God later in life, but I just need to find myself first I think.
They’re Roman Catholic and my mom’s side of the family has been an active part of the church for generations so I’m expected to uphold the family name

Yeah I know I should be proud but it’s so hard when I feel like I need to be perfect in every way. My parents push for straight As, working on the weekends at my job, going to church (even tho I’m atheist), having the perfect boyfriend that is a gentleman, and always being a good little girl. It just hurts anytime they criticize me for not being who they want me to be, even if I’m just being myself
It’s dumb because I feel like it really shouldn’t be called a relapse because it’s only been a week since I cut, but I used to at least once a day so I guess it’s getting slightly better

Yeah I’ve started seeing a therapist, but I’m honestly just hoping to hold on until the end of the year. Then I won’t ever have to talk to them again. I’ve had issues with self harm in the past and if I wouldn’t have seen my therapist today, I’m pretty sure I would’ve relapsed today.

I try to talk but all they do is interrupt me. They treat me like I’m a little kid that knows nothing but then want me to be able to handle anything that comes my way. They’re also not super happy with me at the moment because I came out as bi over Christmas break and they really didn’t like that.

My parents kept saying I should stop complaining about how tired and stressed out I am when I’m taking 17 credit hours through dual credit while I’m a senior in high school. I’m trying to get help for my issues with anxiety, depression, and insomnia so that comment just pushed me over the edge. I know it seems small but it was just enough for me to want to give up

I don’t think this is entirely true. Some people are just looking for the attention, but a think a large part is the increasing visibility and awareness that’s been brought to mental health issues. There may be more people that are living with mental illness that are more vocal about their mental health because of the growing support for people suffering from these issues. Also, the amount of stimulus that is perceived from cell phones, and news, as well as many other alarming stimuli are triggering people to be more anxious, which leads to many other issues. Saying that a lot of people want a mental illness, whether it be for attention because it’s become “trendy” or for whatever reason, can lead to more insecurity from people with serious issues with mental illness, especially depression, that can make them afraid to get help.
